title: A finite ring action on a finite locally constant sheaf is locally constant
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring. Use the constant ring sheaf $\underline\Lambda$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] and the category of its module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $F$ be a sheaf of $\underline\Lambda$-modules. Suppose that its underlying sheaf of sets is finite locally constant: for every object $U$ there is a covering $\{U_i\to U\}$ on each member of which that set sheaf is isomorphic to the constant sheaf of a finite set. Then for every $U$ there is a covering $\{V_j\to U\}$ and finite $\Lambda$-modules $M_j$ such that $F|_{V_j}\simeq\underline{M_j}$ as $\underline\Lambda|_{V_j}$-module sheaves on the localized sites [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. No points or nonempty objects of $\mathcal C$ are assumed.

proof.text: Restrict scalars along the genuine constant-ring sheafification unit eta: const Lambda -> R. This gives a sheaf G with values in ModuleCat Lambda, with exactly the underlying set sheaf of F. Restriction is fully faithful: a Lambda-linear natural map between R-module sheaves is R-linear because every local R-coefficient is locally in the image of eta and the target is separated. In Lean this is scalarSheafFullyFaithful, using Mathlib PresheafOfModules.restrictHomEquivOfIsLocallySurjective.

On each member T of the given actual trivializing cover, apply the finite-operation construction to G restricted to C/T. For a finite label set X, form sections sigma_x using the inverse of the given constant-set isomorphism. Take the finite family consisting of zero, all sums of two labelled sections and all Lambda-multiples. The image sieves of these sections under the constant-set sheafification unit are covering; their finite intersection is covering. This uses Mathlib imageSieve_mem and GrothendieckTopology.finsetInf_mem, with the proved ConstantForget label identities; no site-specific local representation theorem is needed.

On a member of this sieve, take the actual image N of X in the sections. Closure of the finite operation table gives a Lambda-submodule, including zero and negatives via the scalar -1. N is finite because X is finite. Restriction of sections gives a linear natural map from the constant presheaf N to the restricted ModuleCat-valued sheaf. Sheafify it to obtain phi. This is the construction of WeilConjectures/CategoryTheory/Sites/ConstantForget.lean with the finite witness retained, rather than merely concluding IsConstant.

The presheaf map is locally surjective since the constant-set sheafification unit is locally surjective. It is locally injective by representing two elements of N by labels, using the given set-sheaf isomorphism and local injectivity of the constant-set unit; equal labels imply equal actual image elements. The argument allows empty equality sieves and an empty label set. Cancel the locally bijective module-valued sheafification unit to see that phi is an isomorphism. In Lean these are imageSieve_mem, equalizerSieve_mem, the two comp_isLocally..._iff lemmas and Sheaf.isLocallyBijective_iff_isIso.

The recorded constant module realization, after restriction along eta, is the ordinary constant ModuleCat-valued sheaf: its linear unit has the same underlying map as abelian-group sheafification, hence is locally bijective, and its sheafified lift is an isomorphism. Constant sheafification commutes with Over.forget and with the inverse of the iterated-slice equivalence. Transport the finite ModuleCat-valued trivialization to C/W and lift it through the fully faithful scalar-restriction functor to an R-module-sheaf isomorphism F.over W ~= (commutativeSiteConstantModuleFunctor M).over W.

Every covering sieve of the topology generated by J contains an actual J-covering presieve. Prove this by induction on Precoverage.Saturate: original coverings and the maximal sieve are immediate; pullbacks use the covering pullback existence clause of IsSiteForCoverings; transitivity uses bind composition. Apply this to the finite-operation sieve on each original trivializing cover member, and bind the resulting actual covers to the original cover. Each resulting member has the finite module and ringed isomorphism constructed above. No nonempty-object or nonzero-ring assumption is used.
